offer_text: Pay-What-You-Wish Wednesdays: general admission is voluntary-donation every Wednesday from 3 to 9 p.m. Just tell the admissions desk you'd like to participate and give what you like. First Fridays are free general admission, too. (Special exhibitions ticketed separately. The Saguaro's tip: an air-conditioned gallery is a fine place to ride out a July afternoon.)

Community Day, the second Tuesday of every month, is pay-what-you-can admission (8 a.m. to 9 p.m.) — pay $5, $10, $15, or whatever works. Come early or come at dusk; midday among the cactus in summer is a commitment, and I say that with love. (Special ticketed events not included.)

First Friday means free admission to the galleries each month, with live artist demonstrations and every gallery open into the evening. A no-cost, low-sweat way to see world-class Indigenous art. Check the date's posted hours before you head over.

Happy hour runs daily 3 to 7 p.m.: oysters at $2.25, Sea of Cortez wild shrimp at $3, select draft beer $7, wines by the glass $8, house highballs $9, signature cocktails $11, plus a rotation of $11 bites. The seafood flies in fresh daily, so the raw bar is where you want to be.

Happy hour daily on cocktails and wines by the glass 11 a.m. to 6 p.m., with bites layered in from 3 to 6 p.m.: $5 bacon-fat popcorn, $9 featured wines, $12 signature draft cocktails, and shareables up the ladder. A civilized way to ease into a Camelback Corridor evening.

Happy hour Tuesday through Friday, 4 to 6 p.m., in the old Arizona Prohibition Headquarters: $1 off well spirits and domestic beer, $8 prosecco, $8 popcorn, $13 featured specialty cocktails and tacos. An award-winning cocktail program at a downtown-friendly price.

Happy hour at this fourth-floor, Spirited-Award-winning downtown lounge: half-off the bottle & board, $12 spritzes, Negronis, Martinis and wines by the glass, plus daily tacos. Skyline views and serious cocktails without the full nightcap tab.

Twilight rates kick in on afternoon tee times for a lower walk-up green fee on this classic municipal course, and Maricopa County residents can save year-round with the Phoenix Golf Premium and Premium Senior cards. Play the back nine as the sun drops and Camelback goes orange — best light of the day, and the coolest.
